Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (first 100,000 of 124,861 characters). Relevant text: daemon-reload 'Reload the systemd manager configuration'; edit opens 'a drop-in snippet or the main unit file' (default drop-in name override.conf) and afterwards reloads, 'equivalent to systemctl daemon-reload'; cat shows the fragment and drop-ins and warns that on-disk contents 'may differ' from what is loaded without daemon-reload; enable creates the [Install] symlinks and 'does not have the effect of also starting' the unit; is-enabled prints enabled, disabled, static or masked. The exact wording of the status and journal lines in the scenario is an authored rendering.

Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Relevant text: with Restart=on-failure 'the service will be restarted when the process exits with a non-zero exit code'; RestartSec 'Defaults to 100ms'; restarts are 'subject to unit start rate limiting configured with StartLimitIntervalSec= and StartLimitBurst='.

brief.situation: You are the Linux administrator for Ridgeway Supply, a fictional distributor. At 16:15 monitoring reports that exportd.service on fin01 has failed. exportd writes the day's supplier payment file to /srv/export, which the bank collects by SFTP at 17:00.
handover: A colleague tested a new export path for an archive project yesterday.
exportd's unit file comes from the vendor's package in /usr/lib/systemd/system.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the service, its drop-in, boot status, the directory and the pickup.
Each command takes a minute; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close the outage, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The bank collects the file at 17:00, 45 minutes after the 16:15 alert.

writeup.question: For the record: what the logs and unit files showed, why your fix holds, and what you checked before closing.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Uses journalctl for the error (EXPORT_DIR missing, exit status 1, restarts) and systemctl cat to find the drop-in that overrides the unit.
parts.modelAnswer: journalctl -u exportd showed 'EXPORT_DIR /srv/export-old: No such file or directory' and the restarts; systemctl cat showed the override.conf drop-in setting that path over the unit's /srv/export.

parts.label: Fix
parts.criteria: Corrects or removes the drop-in (not the vendor file, which the drop-in overrides and an update overwrites), makes systemd load it (systemctl edit reloads; a manual edit needs daemon-reload), starts it, and enables it for boot.
parts.modelAnswer: systemctl edit put EXPORT_DIR=/srv/export in the override and reloaded systemd; then start, and enable because yesterday's test left it disabled. Editing /usr/lib would change nothing while the drop-in overrides it, and creating /srv/export-old would write the file where the bank never looks.

parts.label: Verified
parts.criteria: Checks the file is in /srv/export before 17:00 and the unit's state.
parts.modelAnswer: ls showed payments-today.csv in /srv/export before 17:00; status active, is-enabled enabled.

restored.headline: Good: fixed where systemd reads it
restored.body: You read the journal and the unit files first, changed the drop-in that overrode the unit, let systemd load it, checked the file, and re-enabled the service so a reboot cannot undo the day.

scoring.modelReasoning: systemctl status shows a drop-in and a disabled unit. journalctl -u exportd shows exit status 1 because EXPORT_DIR=/srv/export-old does not exist, and Restart=on-failure retrying until the start rate limit. systemctl cat shows yesterday's override.conf setting that path; drop-ins are parsed after the unit file, so editing /usr/lib/systemd/system/exportd.service changes nothing. systemctl edit exportd fixes the override and reloads (removing it by hand needs systemctl daemon-reload). Start it, enable it (yesterday's test disabled it), and check /srv/export before the 17:00 pickup. Creating /srv/export-old would make it run but write where the bank never looks.
